messages:
Nina: Ran a micro-replay where two tenants continually compete for the same slab and we see churn: demote -> parallel rehydrates -> eviction flurry. Low QPS but p99 spikes. Anyone else hit this under pooling?
Raj: I reproduced briefly. The handoff path seems to allocate eviction credits at enqueue time; if multiple enqueues occur in-flight they can oversubscribe credits before any start.
Sam: That explains it. Cheap fix is to only debit credits when prefill actually begins, but that has a race where two starters begin concurrently and still oversubscribe. Need a reservation mechanism.
Elena: Proposal: lightweight atomic reservation via CAS on slab.fill_epoch. Reserve at enqueue, keep reservation_id in the queue entry; consume at start. If a retry happens, reuse same resv_id so we don't double-count.
Nina: Sketch: reserve CAS bumps a small reservation bit and returns a 8-bit id. We keep `reservations` as ephemeral in slab metadata with short TTL.
Sam: Pseudocode:
```
// reserve
old = slab.fill_epoch
if CAS(&slab.fill_epoch, old, old+1<<8) -> resv = extract(old)
enqueue(entry.with_resv(resv))
// start
if entry.resv == slab.current_resv -> debit_credit()
else drop/retry
```
Elena: Important: persistence/heartbeat. If a node crashes after reserving but before start, TTL must reclaim. Also epoch monotonicity across restarts is needed. Suggest we incorporate epoch bumps in the lease heartbeat to survive short restarts.
Raj: Also add dedupe: `(tenant_id, demote_epoch)` stored on the slab to avoid re-enqueueing the same demote multiple times. That prevents duplicate prefills when demote is retried.
Nina: Metrics to add: `slab.resv_active_count`, `slab.demote_dedup_hits`, `handshake_resv_reclaims`. Ops rule: if resv_reclaims > 0.1% for 15m, autoswitch pool_reservation_enabled=false.
Sam: For perf: keep CAS word 64-bit: high 48 bits epoch, low bits flags/resv_count — single cacheline. Avoid per-slab locks.
Elena: Tests: unit for reservation CAS, integration sim with reordered RPCs and node crash after reserve, and a 1h chaos job with heavy small-tenant sweeps.
Nina: I'll own the canary rollout plan. Flag: `pool_reservation_enabled`. Start on a 4-node canary pool with traffic replay; 6h stable -> expand.
Raj: I'll proto code and add the new metrics. Sam, can you produce a compact replay that reproduces the leak pattern so we can iterate fast?
Sam: Yep. I'll also add a short rate-limited log when a reservation is reclaimed: one-line with slab_id/resv_id/age.
monitor-bot: alert-configured: eng-runtime.slab.resv_reclaim_rate warn=0.001
Elena: One more guard: allow SLA-tagged tenants to preempt reservations within a small steal window (e.g., 50ms) to avoid blocking high-priority traffic. Rank by priority bits in the resv word.
Nina: Sounds good. TL;DR: add CAS-based reservation, TTL reclaim, demote dedupe by epoch, new metrics/alerts, and canary flag. I'll write the spec + runbook and open the PR.
Raj: Thanks — will sync on implementation after the spec.
